subject: ENGLISH
title: Blend Builders · M01 D13
objective: Read taught consonant blends while keeping their component sounds perceptible.
introduction: Put two letter sounds together and read words like stop and flag. Say the blend and keep both sounds!

vocabulary.definition: A letter that is not a vowel, like b, c, or d.
To join letter sounds together to read a word.
Something you hear; in the blend st, you hear both /s/ and /t/.

activities.instruction: Hear how st and fl keep both letter sounds!
activities.content: In a consonant blend, neighboring consonant sounds can still be heard.

feedback.correct: Nice work. Continue to the next step.

items.prompt: Which word begins with two consonant sounds?
items.explanation: In stop you can hear /s/ then /t/ — that is the st blend. Ship begins with sh, one sound, and chair begins with ch, one sound.

items.prompt: Which word begins with a consonant blend?
items.explanation: Flag begins with fl: you can hear both /f/ and /l/. Ship begins with sh, one sound together, and top starts with just /t/.

items.prompt: Which word does NOT begin with a blend?
items.explanation: Ship starts with sh — one sound you cannot split. Flag (fl) and stop (st) are blends because you can hear both letters.

items.prompt: Which word begins with the st blend?
items.explanation: Stop begins with st: say it slowly and you hear /s/ then /t/. Ship starts with sh, and top starts with just /t/.

items.prompt: Which word starts with a consonant blend?
items.explanation: Star begins with the blend st, which blends the sounds /s/ and /t/. Ship begins with the digraph sh, and egg begins with a vowel.
